messages:
support_jen: ACME on hosted API reporting intermittent 504s and 5xx for /v1/generate since ~14:22 UTC. They say p99 token latency jumps and their client retries, amplifying load. sample req_id=acme-req-7f2b, tenant=acme, region=us-west1
kevin-sre: pulling metrics now. p95 token latency for pool=hosted-1 rose from 120ms -> 420ms around 14:21. queue_depth metric shows spike to 1024 (our configured hard limit) with enqueue_drops = 4800 in 5m window.
maria-eng: I can repro locally-ish. Continuous-batcher backlog: small requests with long sequence tokens are creating very skewed batches and stalling KV cache warmups. Logs show enqueue failures and workers pinned on single large seqs.
kevin-sre: logs please — any request IDs?
maria-eng: paste below (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17T14:20:59Z] ERROR enqueue failed tenant=acme pool=hosted-1 req=acme-req-7f2b err=queue_full
[2026-03-17T14:21:03Z] WARN batch_worker tenant=acme batch_id=bd-993 size=48 avg_seq=1320 processing_ms=16320
[2026-03-17T14:21:04Z] WARN kvcache miss tenant=acme key=pref-0 warmup_ms=15000
[2026-03-17T14:21:11Z] ERROR dispatch timeout tenant=acme req=acme-req-7f2b err=deadline_exceeded
```
ryan-support: Customer is on a tight SLA; they’ve started retrying on 5xx which is making tail worse. They've asked for ETA and mitigation now.
infra-eli: Immediate mitigations we can do: 1) increase pool max_queue_depth for hosted-1 (temporary), 2) enable tenant admission limits to throttle ACME, 3) route ACME to a lighter model variant (if available) as fallback. I can do 1 and 2 now.
kevin-sre: Agree. Also runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/queue-saturation (see section "eviction and soft-throttle"). Follow low-risk path first.
maria-eng: Repro steps I used to simulate: send 200rps per-tenant of small payloads that expand into long token sequences due to prompt templates. Example script: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"<long system prompt>...","max_tokens":1024}' &
done
```
kevin-sre: I'm going to patch hosted-1 config to bump max_queue_depth -> 2048 for 15m window, roll it back after stabilizing. Will also toggle tenant throttle for acme to 50rps burst.
deploy-bot: config-change: staging -> prod PATCH /configs/pools/hosted-1 applied by infra-eli at 1745556810. Change: {"max_queue_depth":2048} (id=chg-942)
ops-bot: alert: queue_depth spike cleared to 610 after change; enqueue_drops dropping toward 0. (alert_id=alert-8812)
kevin-sre: After change p95 token latency down to ~180ms, p99 still elevated at ~1.2s. We're seeing fewer 504s. Need to keep an eye for retry floods.
ryan-support: Notified ACME support and CSM. Customer acknowledges mitigation but wants a root cause and timeline.
acme-csm: Thanks — please ping when we have postmortem and permanent fix plan. They are concerned about repeated incidents.
maria-eng: Next steps for permanent: implement tenant-aware admission control that shorts large-seq requests or routes them to dedicated capacity; improve batcher eviction policy to avoid single long seq starving others; add per-tenant queue backing metrics to console.\e kevin-sre: created incident ticket INC-2026-174555 with checklist: chronology, metrics (p95/p99), config diff chg-942, customer communication. Assigning follow-up to eng-runtime.
support_jen: Thanks team — I'll keep ACME updated and will attach logs + req ids. Leaving notes in the ticket. :thumbsup:
kevin-sre: tagging for postmortem: @maria-eng @infra-eli. Please capture timeline and the trigger (prompt template + retry behaviour).
maria-eng: will do. Also proposing a short-term policy: if pool queue_depth > 80% for > 1m, automatically enable soft-throttle per-tenant and reduce batching window for new batches.
ryan-support: I'll propose that to customer as an upcoming improvement.
deploy-bot: followup: rolled change chg-942 back to 1024 at 1745557600 (scheduled rollback) — monitor and prepare to extend if stable.
kevin-sre: closing interim mitigation; leaving incident open for postmortem and engineering follow-ups.
support_jen: customer updated at 14:45 UTC, they reported fewer errors. Will capture final notes once PMs sign off.
